title: Memory Leak Mitigation in Long-Running Agents
summary: Bound retained state and resource lifetimes so long-running agents remain stable as conversations, tools, and tenants accumulate.
overview: Memory leak mitigation addresses resources that remain reachable or allocated after their useful lifetime. Agent runtimes are especially exposed because conversation histories, tool transcripts, callback closures, streaming buffers, and background tasks can survive many turns. GPU memory adds a separate distinction between live tensors, cached allocator blocks, and key-value cache retained for active sequences.

A rising resident-set size is a symptom rather than proof of a leak. Capacity growth, allocator fragmentation, unbounded caches, native-library allocations, and true lost ownership require different remedies. The architectural goal is explicit ownership, bounded cardinality, and observable release at session, request, and worker boundaries.

production.poc: A prototype should run repeated conversations in one process and measure whether retained objects return toward a stable baseline.
production.production: Production introduces session expiration, bounded caches, stream cancellation, task ownership, and memory-aware admission limits.
production.scale: Enterprise operation adds long-duration soak tests, per-tenant quotas, heap sampling, and controlled worker recycling as a containment mechanism while root causes are repaired.

components.name: Session store
components.role: Keeps durable history outside the worker and loads only the required turn window.

components.name: Resource scope manager
components.role: Closes clients, cancels child tasks, and releases buffers when a request ends.

components.name: Bounded cache
components.role: Enforces byte and entry limits with eviction and expiry rather than unlimited memoization.

components.name: Memory profiler
components.role: Separates heap objects, native allocation, process residency, and accelerator allocation.

components.name: Admission controller
components.role: Limits concurrent contexts using measured memory cost, not request count alone.

flow.title: Assign ownership
flow.description: Attach every tool stream, task, and temporary artifact to an explicit request or session scope.

flow.title: Load a bounded working set
flow.description: Retrieve current context while keeping full history in durable external storage.

flow.title: Observe growth
flow.description: Record memory before and after representative turns and correlate with session and token counts.

flow.title: Close the scope
flow.description: Cancel unfinished tasks, release stream readers, and remove callbacks when the caller disconnects or the task ends.

flow.title: Evict and expire
flow.description: Remove idle sessions and cache entries under byte budgets and tenant limits.

flow.title: Contain abnormal workers
flow.description: Drain and replace a worker exceeding its memory envelope while retaining diagnostic evidence.

diagrams.caption: External history and explicit request ownership prevent completed turns from remaining attached to a worker indefinitely.

useCase.title: A dispatch assistant that stays active across shifts
useCase.situation: Dispatchers keep long conversations open while checking routes, driver status, and delivery exceptions.
useCase.problem: Workers retain every tool response and disconnected stream listener, so memory grows across shift changes.
useCase.requirement: Support ongoing conversations while bounding each worker footprint and preserving cancellation behavior.
useCase.architecture: The service stores full transcripts in a database, loads a compact working window, and scopes tracking streams to active requests.
runtime: A dispatcher opens a vehicle-status stream and later closes the browser.
Disconnect propagation cancels the stream, removes callbacks, and expires the idle session cache.
useCase.failure: If a native map library continues growing outside the managed heap, the worker drains while profiles identify the native allocation path.
useCase.impact: Measure memory per active session, retained bytes after cancellation, and out-of-memory termination rate; worker restarts are containment rather than evidence of a repaired leak.

tradeoffs.cost: Adds read latency and serialization overhead.
May increase model or data-fetch work.

tradeoffs.benefit: Limits the duration of an unresolved leak.
tradeoffs.cost: Interrupts warm caches and can conceal the underlying defect.

failures.detection: Heap snapshots show completed requests reachable through listeners.
failures.recovery: Unregister handlers in a guaranteed cleanup path.

failures.scenario: Concurrent long contexts exhaust GPU memory
failures.detection: Cache occupancy and active-token counts rise before allocation errors.
failures.recovery: Reduce admission and safely cancel or defer excess sequences.

mistakes.fix: Measure native and accelerator allocations alongside application objects.

mistakes.mistake: Capping cache entries but not bytes
mistakes.fix: Apply byte budgets because transcript and embedding sizes vary.

mistakes.mistake: Clearing all memory on a timer
mistakes.fix: Use ownership and expiry policies that preserve active requests.

whenToUse: Use for persistent agents, streaming tools, and long-lived workers.
Use when memory correlates with cumulative turns rather than current load.
Use before increasing concurrency for long-context inference.
whenNotToUse: Do not treat expected allocator caching as a confirmed leak.
Avoid indiscriminate eviction of active sequence state.
Do not rely exclusively on larger containers to mask unbounded growth.
checklist: Define request and session resource owners.
Cap transcript bytes held in memory.
Capture profiles before recycling anomalous workers.
